remarks: Are you buying, or shall I weigh your opinions?
The fish seller says his catch came in this morning. So did his grandfather, if you believe him.
Watch his thumb on the scales next door. The man sells more thumb than mullet.
Fresh fish should smell of the sea. His smells of a theological dispute left in the sun.
They settled the Union in Florence. Nobody thought to settle it with the customers in my queue.
My brother supports the Union. My mother does not. Sunday dinner now requires a mediator.
Greek or Latin, everyone expects the baker to rise before dawn.
I asked the priest whether short measure was a sin. He asked whose scales I meant.
My wife has taken to praising the dyer. Apparently he understands colour. I have questions about his other talents.
The dyer brought my wife a ribbon. I have sent him an invoice.
My wife says I hear only what suits me. An excellent woman. Always praising my judgement.
The Emperor should visit the market more often. We could tell him exactly where the money goes.
If you see the Emperor, tell him the tax collector has already been. Twice. He seems to have forgotten the first visit.
You have the look of someone accustomed to giving orders. Try giving one for a sack of barley.
Such a fine cloak. Shall I name a price for you, or for your steward?
No, the imperial eagle above my stall does not mean the palace pays my rent.
That sack is heavy. I can fetch a porter, or you can discover how strong your convictions are.
My prices are written plainly. The bargaining begins when you pretend you cannot read them.
Credit? Certainly. Bring someone richer than yourself to guarantee it.
I know three men who claim to have spoken with the Sultan. They owe me money between them.
The Genoese buy in bulk, the Venetians bargain in bulk. I prefer the ones who pay.
There is a rumour that grain will be cheaper tomorrow. I believe the man spreading it wants mine today.
Mind the cat. She works here. The boy is merely related to me.
My apprentice can count to a hundred. After that, he starts calling the difference providence.
Take the beans. Your household will eat well, though your neighbours may hear about it.
That loaf is for the widow by the fountain. Choose another; I have put it aside.
The old soldier gets his measure first. He has waited for his pay quite long enough.
People tell me everything at this stall. Then they ask whether I know any news.
You keep looking at me as though I ought to say something memorable. Buy something. I shall remember that.
Go on, take a pinch and judge for yourself. I can endure an honest customer.
